# Ditdah

> Morse code, one dit at a time. Ditdah is a free web app that teaches the full Morse alphabet plus numbers and symbols using picture and sound mnemonics, with sending practice, by-ear receiving practice, a Koch-method course, a CW QSO simulator, translator, and arcade games.

Ditdah is a single-page application: all features live at the root URL (https://ditdah.me/). There are no other crawlable paths — do not invent URLs beyond the root.

Key features:

- Send mode: practice keying Morse via keyboard, on-screen buttons, single-key input, or a straight key.
- Receive mode: learn to copy by ear, progressing from letters to words to full sentences, with XP, levels, and badges.
- Koch-method course: a structured 39-lesson curriculum that builds character recognition at full speed.
- On the air: a CW QSO simulator with 20 authentic HF scenarios plus a CW shorthand guide.
- Translator: bidirectional text-to-Morse and Morse-to-text conversion.
- Arcade games: Signal Squadron and Cave of Echoes.
- Adjustable character speed, effective (Farnsworth) speed, and tone.
- Strong accessibility: one-switch scanning, visual and haptic flash output, and experimental gaze input.
- Optional account sync to keep progress across devices.

Ditdah is a remake of AceCentre's open-source "Morse Learn" project (Apache-2.0), with attribution.

## App

- [Ditdah](https://ditdah.me/): The app itself — learning, practice, games, and settings all in one page.

## Related

- [CallSignReady](https://callsignready.com): Companion app by the same author for studying for the Ham Radio Technician license.
